THE LINE: a uewf tenure is warranted where a held document BILLS THE ENTITY AS THAT FEDERATION'S OWN, or STAGES IT FOR ONE OF THAT FEDERATION'S OWN CHAMPIONSHIPS. Entry to a tournament held at an interfederation event is not by itself enough — the Summit's tournaments were open to all comers and a bracket slot says only that somebody entered. WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW: his own manager announces his withdrawal from the federation in that federation's name — Ace Diamond, interviewed on the WeWF's newsdesk of 15 February 1992: "I have decided to pull my Brimstone Baxter and Cannonball Calhoun out of the UeWF." You cannot be pulled out of a federation you were not in. The same manager's letter of 4 March lists among his stable's credentials that Baxter "finished in the top 5 at the Royal Rumble", which is the Summit's event and would not on its own have earned this tenure.

caption: The other half of Da Boyz, a knee specialist who took the Ultimate Lanny’s legs out from under him at the second Summit and, the following June, won the PWA’s own inaugural Tag Team Championship and held it until the Dogs of War took it.
notes: Merged from nunzio-summit, superseding this row’s earlier “nothing beyond the name ties them” filing, which the documents refute. Receipt: the Summit of E-Wrestling’s own third night of 29 December 1991 books “Da Boyz, Guido and Nunzio of the WeWF” with “Da Boss” at ringside; the PWA’s own 1992 record announces “Approaching the Ring led by their manager Da Boss, DA BOYZ” and books them against the Shield Brothers out of Russell, Ontario — the same team name, the same two members, the same manager, and the same opponents the Summit’s own card had staged. The PWA tenure above is folded in from that row; data/aliases.json redirects the retired id to this one.
